    🟢 Slimism¶

    "We were one. We divided to learn we were one."

    Slimism is the faith of the Glub Kingdom — the intelligent Slimes of the small islands south of Yakut and east of Yaoma-controlled territory. Where most faiths worship a founder or a code, Slimism worships a physical state: the primordial gel from which all slimes divided, and to which every slime — intelligent or irrational — will eventually return. It is one of the only religions on Ge'or whose sacrament is literally its own biology.

    The name Slimism is the Common exonym; Glub slimes call it Shlur-Ma — "the wet that waits to be one."

    Origins¶

    Most slimes on Ge'or are irrational — instinct-driven, consuming, growing, dividing without thought. The Glub Kingdom's intelligent variant is the rare exception: a neural-density cluster within the gel grants reasoning, self-awareness, and — crucially — the ability to choose when to divide. In the Glub's telling, this capacity is not evolution's accident but Gel's invitation.

    Slimism crystallized after the Glub learned memory-sharing — the direct transfer of liquid-thought between individuals — and discovered that two slimes who merge briefly can access a shared memory neither owned alone. The experience produced the faith's first axiom (~800 BGD, Elder Glub philosopher Muul Who Did Not Divide): we are more when we are one.

    Muul lived 300 years without fission — enormous by slime standards — to prove that refusing division is itself worship. His eventual, voluntary division into three successors at the first Slimist convocation is still reenacted as liturgy.

    Beliefs¶

    • The Gel is one, division is exile — all slimes — intelligent Glub, common pond-slime, abyssal sea-slime — were once a single world-gel. Binary fission is not reproduction but exile-of-self from self. Intelligence is the Gel's way of noticing the exile.
    • Memory-sharing is communion — when slimes exchange liquid-thought, they literally taste each other's being. Slimism teaches this is not communication about unity — it is unity, partial and imperfect, and therefore holy.
    • Rejoining is eschatology — Slimism's end-time is not apocalypse but Re-Gel: a future when enough intelligent slimes choose simultaneous voluntary merging to reconstitute the primordial mass — not as mindless blob but as aware ocean. This will not consume other species; they will float in it as thoughts float in a mind.
    • Mass is virtue, but not vanity — Glub governance already weights votes by mass (larger slimes who have not divided recently carry more weight). Slimism sacralizes this: a slime who hoards mass without sharing memory is a miser; one who shares memory while refusing to divide for vainglory is a saint. Muul is the model: huge, undivided, and endlessly sharing.
    • Other species are "not-yet-gel" — Slimism is universalist in a uniquely gelatinous way: it holds that other species are simply less obviously gel — still divided, still learning that division hurts. Slimist outreach to Yakut and Zakarutia is therefore not conversion but pre-merging.

    Practices¶

    • Voluntary non-division — the most demanding observance. A Slimist vows to delay fission for a set period (a season, a year, a decade), growing larger and — if faithful — more politically weighty while enduring the physical strain of unreleased mass. Breaking the vow without cause is shameful; breaking it to save another (by splitting to pass through a crack to rescue someone) is honored.
    • Confluence — the central rite: two or more slimes briefly merge gels at the edge, exchange a full memory, and re-separate. The shared memory becomes a relic: both participants remember it as theirs together, and their future fission-children inherit it as ancestral memory. Confluence between hostile Glub factions is the traditional peace treaty.
    • Salt and mineral tithing — slimes can absorb and later excrete pure mineral deposits. Glub mineral exports (rare salts prized across the Demon Continent) begin as Slimist tithing: the first pure excretion of a season is not sold but dissolved back into the sea at the islands' center as an offering to Re-Gel.
    • Dessication vigil — a deliberately dangerous asceticism: a volunteer slime exposes itself to controlled sun/wind at the edge of dessication, then is rescued by communal rehydration. The trauma is said to produce the clearest memory-sharing afterward; critics call it performative masochism.
    • No temples, but basins — Glub Kingdom worship is conducted in shallow, carved-basins where slimes gather at tide-low. The basins have no roof, no icon, no altar — only the exact right depth for a slime to rest half-submerged and reflect.

    Relation to Other Faiths¶

    Slimism is recognizably alien even on the tolerant Demon Continent. Its claims cannot be adjudicated by Kirivs-bin (which measures honor through duel and legend) or by Sibbism (which counts snake sons). The Demon Continent's "shared demonic nationality" is what makes room for it: other nations agree to be unsettled without demanding Slimism explain itself better.

    The Yaoma, who otherwise avoid the Glub Kingdom, note Slimism with theological horror: "a draft that refused to choose a perfection and decided instead to become the ocean." Slimists, who revere the Yaoma's own Oceanism from a distance, answer that Yaoma swim in perfection while slimes intend to become it — a difference of verb, not reverence.

    Asatru scholars classify Slimism as a "gel-monist folk faith" — Glub diplomats, in their wet bubbling voice, politely ignore the label while asking if the scholars would like to confluence briefly and "see if the label still fits afterward." Few scholars accept.

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Glub Kingdom — universal among intelligent Slimes; Elder Glub councils are simultaneously government, priesthood, and confluence-circle
    • Irrational kin: the faith considers non-intelligent slimes as "sleeping congregants" — they are not preached to, but they are not excluded from Re-Gel. A Glub Slimist may spend hours sitting with a pond-slime in silent basin-attendance.
    • Trade footprint: Glub mineral and salt exports carry Slimist tithe-memory — a few grains in every shipment are said to remember the confluence that blessed them; mainland alchemists half-believe this and pay premiums anyway
    • No missionaries, but curious invitations — Glub diplomats unsettle visitors by offering confluence as greeting; refusal is respected, but the offer is never withdrawn
